**Title:** CNMS-E7501, HNBR, OSI 22x48-4 for Packer Elements, 90 Durometer, Unified Spec

## 1.0 Scope:

This specification is for a hydrogenated nitrile compound for use as packer elements. This specification is for hydrogenated nitrile parts and compounds formulated from HNBR polymers supplied by Lanxess (Therban) or Zeon Chemicals (Zetpol). It is not for HNBR polymer purchased for compounding by Schlumberger.

## 2.0 Requirements

### 2.1 Material:
Shall be Oil States compound 22x48-4. Parts purchased under this specification shall be a hydrogenated nitrile rubber compound, formulated and cured to meet the required physical and mechanical properties.

### 2.2 Manufacture:
Production elements shall be molded from compounded stock. Machining is limited to flash removal not dimensional control. Test parts may be machined in accordance with 100218311 - Use of Molded and Machined Packer Elements. To achieve a void free component, it is sometimes necessary to vacuum compression mold certain elements in accordance with 100120278 - CNMS-12, Specification for Processing Packer Elements By Vacuum Molding.

### 2.3 RoHS and WEEE:
Material shall not contain any element in reportable limits in accordance with the regulations of RoHS and WEEE. The certification should contain a notation that the part complies with these standards.

Note: WEEE is applicable only for Electrical and Electronic parts.

### 2.4 Testing:
Samples of finished elements or raw material taken according to a sample plan shall conform to specification requirements when tested according to the applicable procedures.

### 2.5 Physical and Mechanical Properties shall conform to:

| Property                                         | Requirement  | ASTM Spec  |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------------ | ---------- |
| Tensile Strength, psi minimum                    | 2000         | D-412      |
| Tensile Stress (Modulus) at 100%, psi minimum    | 1000         | D-412      |
| Elongation % minimum                             | 125          | D-412      |
| Hardness, Durometer A                            | 90 +/- 5     | D-2240     |
| Compression Set 70 hours at 212°F (100°C), % max | 35           | D-395      |
| Specific Gravity                                 | 1.33 +/- .02 | D-792      |
| Tear Resistance, Die C, ppi minimum              | 150          | ASTM D-624 |


### 2.6 Responsibility for Inspection:
The supplier is responsible for performing and reporting the physical and mechanical tests required by this specification. The purchaser requires the supplier to furnish samples necessary to ensure that these parts conform to the requirements of this specification or to evaluate performance in products.

## 1. Scope:

This specification is for a hydrogenated nitrile compound 22x27-11 from Oil States primarily for use as packer elements, although not restricted to that product form and usage.

Oil States compound 22x27-11 for packer elements. Parts purchased under this specification shall be a hydrogenated nitrile rubber compound, formulated and cured to meet the required physical and mechanical properties

2.2.2 Compound: 22x27-11

### 2.3 Manufacture:
Elements shall be vacuum molded from compounded stock.

### 2.4 RoHS, and WEEE:
Material shall not contain any element in reportable limits in accordance with the regulations of RoHS and WEEE. The certification should contain a notation that the part complies with these standards.

Note: WEEE is applicable only for Electrical and Electronic parts.

2.5.1 Random samples of finished elements or raw material taken according to a sample plan shall conform to the specification requirements when tested according to ASTM D-1414 or to the applicable procedure in so far as practical.

2.5.2 Physical and mechanical properties shall conform to the below requirements.

| Properties                                   | Requirement  | ASTM Spec |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------ | --------- |
| Tensile Strength, psi. min.                  | 3000         | D-412     |
| Tensile Stress at 100% Elongation, psi. min. | 232          | D-412     |
| Elongation, % min.                           | 400          | D-412     |
| Hardness, Durometer A                        | 70 ± 5       | D-2240    |
| Specific Gravity                             | 1.15.to 1.19 | D-792     |
| Tear Resistance, Die C, ppi, min.            | 220          | D-624     |
| Compression Set, 70 hrs. at 212°F (100°C), % | Report       | D-395     |

**Title:** CSP-146, Ion Nitriding of Nickel Based Alloys

## 1.0 Scope:

1.1 This specification is for Ion Nitriding by use of glow discharge in a partial vacuum. Ammonia gas nitriding cannot be used as a substitute for this process.

1.2 An alternate S-phase nitriding of Ni-based alloys process (101888180) is acceptable as long as it meets effective case depth requirements.

1.3 The resulting surface has improved hardness, wear, and galling resistance.

1.4 The effective case depth will vary from 0.00020" to 0.00060" depending on alloy and part thickness. This specification covers alloy 925, 935, 718, 725.

Note: Effective case depth is generally defined as a distance from the surface to the diffusion zone where hardness falls below 50 HRc (converted from 542 Knoop/ 513 Vickers). Additional testing may be requested on the drawing to prove the exact case depth.

# Title: CSP-146, Ιon Νitriding of Νickel Based Αlloys

# 3.0 Test Coupons

3.3 The dimensions of the test coupon should be at least 1” diameter round stock by 1” in height. Larger test coupons are acceptable as long as at least 1” in height. The test coupons shall have similar surface finish as the part area being nitrided.

3.4 The test coupons shall be properly identified and shall reference the SLB parts to be nitrided. Methods of identification (e.g., SLB purchase order number, job number, etc) shall be determined by the SLB supplier (machine shop, applicator).

NOTE: The applicator shall not process any parts without test coupons unless utilizing sacrificial part(s).

# 4.0 Personnel Requirement

4.1 Personnel performing the nitriding operation shall be qualified by the applicator (coating shop) using a documented process that includes training and competency checks.

4.2 If properly qualified personnel are unavailable to perform the required quality-control tests, an external Metallurgical Service Laboratories with established credentials (e.g., ISO compliant lab) shall be used. In order to determine appropriate nitriding, test coupons shall be sectioned, mounted, ground, and polished.

# 5.0 Equipment Requirements

5.1 Ion (plasma) nitriding shall be conducted with a mixture of hydrogen and nitrogen gas. The applicator (coating shop) shall retain copies of the gas certificates.

5.2 The equipment used by the applicator for process and product acceptance shall be calibrated at documented intervals using standards traceable to ΝΙSΤ or equivalent national or international standard.

# 6.0 Process Requirements

6.1 Parts to be nitrided shall be completely free of grease, oil, and other hydrocarbon-based compound and any other contaminants. Suitable equipment shall be used to completely degrease and clean the entire part prior to nitriding. All cleaning agents shall be free of compounds that would inhibit nitriding.

6.2 Nitriding shall not be performed without masking per the requirements defined on the engineering drawing. If the part is to be completely nitrided the drawing must clearly indicate "Νo Μasking Required". Applicator shall identify area(s) to be used for fixturing or supporting the part. The fixturing shall follow a written procedure or diagram provided by applicator.

6.2.1 Areas to be masked shall be identified on the drawing and shall be masked by mechanical means (such as plates or other covers) or copper paint compound such as Condursal Ν9W. Note: Condursal containing copper is not available in the UK. The equivalent UK version of Condursal Ν9W is acceptable.

6.3 The applicator shall have a documented procedure detailing the process cycle times to be used for the different alloy types to provide required nitrided case depth.

#### 4.4.1. Heat Treating Equipment Qualification and Calibration

1. The practice for qualification of heat-treating equipment shall be per the API 6A annex for qualification of heat-treating equipment, AMS 2750, or another internationally recognized standard

2. Furnace instrumentation shall be calibrated at least every 3 months with acceptable grace period as defined in AMS 2750 or other internationally recognized standard.

# 4.4.3. Solution Annealing and Age Hardening

The production material and QTC(s) shall be solution annealed and age hardened in accordance with following procedure. Heat treatment shall be performed only by producing mill. Local heat treatment shall be allowed only with written authorization by Schlumberger and following a written procedure.

# 4.4.3.1. Solution Annealing

Solution anneal at temperature 1870⁰F to 1925⁰F (1021⁰C to 1052⁰C), for one (1) hour minimum to two and half (2 ½) hours maximum. Cool in air, inert gas, water, polymer, or oil to ambient temperature.

Note: Air cooling or inert gas cooling of section thickness greater than 3 in. (76 mm) shall only be upon agreement between purchaser, manufacturer and end user.

# 4.4.3.2. Age Hardening

Age harden at temperature 1425⁰F to 1475⁰F (774⁰C to 802⁰C) for six to eight (6 to 8) hours. Cool in air, inert gas, water, polymer or oil to ambient temperature.

# 4.4.4. Re-heat Treatment

1. Complete re-heat treatment is permitted. Alternatively, re-aging within the parameters of section 4.4.3.2 is permitted, provided the cumulative aging time does not exceed the maximum allowable aging time.
2. If the material is re-aged without re-solution annealing, the testing required by 4.5.1, 4.5.2, 0, 4.5.5 may be performed on remnants of the original QTC, provided the remnants are re-aged with the production material they represent.
3. All other requirements required by 4.5.1, 4.5.2, 4.5.3, 4.5.5 shall be met by material that has been subjected to either of above re-heat treatment steps.

4.5.2. Impact Toughness

4.5.2.1. Test Location and Frequency

Charpy V-notch impact testing shall be performed in accordance with ASTM A370 or E23. All tests shall be performed at or below –75 °F (–60 °C). # 4.5.5. Microstructural Analysis Requirements

# 4.5.5.1. Test Location and Method

The microstructural analysis sample(s) shall be taken from a QTC from each remelting ingot per heat treat lot. The QTC shall be either a prolongation (full cross-section on thickest end) or sacrificial production part. The microstructural analysis shall be performed on material in the final heat treatment condition. Refer Attachment A-1 for sample locations.

The microstructural samples shall be etched using one of the approved etchants as shown in Attachment B.

# 4.5.5.2. Grain Size Evaluation

1. The average grain size shall be determined in accordance with ASTM E112. The ASTM average grain size shall be No. 2 or finer.
2. No topological duplex grain size, as defined and measured per ASTM E1181, is allowed.

# 4.5.5.3. Deleterious Phases Examination

The microstructural samples shall be examined for deleterious phases at 100Χ and 500Χ using light microscopy. The acceptance criteria are as follows:

1. The microstructure shall be free from acicular phases except in individual, isolated grains that are not representative of the bulk microstructure. In no case shall any individual grain be surrounded with acicular phases.
2. The microstructures shall be free from continuous networks of secondary phases along grain boundaries, except for individual, isolated grains or isolated fields of view that are not representative of the bulk microstructure. The presence of discrete, isolated particles of secondary phases or carbides is acceptable.
3. There shall be no Laves phase.

Examples of acceptable and unacceptable microstructures are provided in Attachment C-1 through C-5. These examples are intended to portray the representative microstructure and not worst-case fields, and they do not represent all of the possible precipitation patterns in Alloy 718. Therefore, these examples are not intended to be quantitative standards of cleanliness. C-1 and C-2 are examples of acceptable microstructures. C-3, C-4, and C-5 are examples of unacceptable microstructures.

The site audit should be conducted by the Supplier Quality Manager or an authorized auditor. It is mandatory for the auditor to document the list of equipment used for production, details of the production processes (both internal and external), quality and process control procedures and the test equipment used for quality control. The coating suppliers shown on this list at the first release (January 2010) have been added based on historical purchase records, existing qualification records and recommendations from authorized personnel in the Materials group. ## 5 Prior to Assembly

### 5.1 General

Ensure all the required tools and reference documents are on hand. Verify that there is a complete balance of parts on hand and that all serial numbers have been documented.

### 5.2 Component Parts

Inspect each chemical injection port on the mandrel (1) using a bore scope. The port(s) should be free of any foreign matter including grease, cutting fluid, dirt, debris, etc. The surface in the chemical injection port(s) should be smooth and free of any significant scratches or imperfections. If any foreign matter is seen during the visual inspection, clean the chemical injection port(s) using an aerosol degreaser and compressed air. Re-inspect using a bore scope and repeat as necessary to remove all foreign matter prior to proceeding. If scratches or imperfections are noticed in the chemical injection port(s), return the mandrel to the inspection department and request verification that the surface finish is within the parameters specified on the mandrel drawing.

# INJECTION LINE TEST PRESSURE (PSI)

1. Increase injection line pressure to the INJECTION LINE TEST PRESSURE +/- 100 psi. Allow pressure to stabilize, hold, monitor, and record injection line pressure and internal pressure trace for 15 minutes. The pressure change should be less than 1% of the test pressure in the last 15 minutes.

3. Bleed internal pressure.
4. Remove bore seal plugs or test caps. Remove DCIN II or HPHT DCIN II pressure test kit.

## 1. Scope:

1.1 This specification is for AISI 4140 / 4142 / 4145 Mod bars and tubes furnished in pre-heat treated condition, normalized quench and tempered or quench and tempered to 110,000 psi (759 MPa) minimum yield strength.

1.2 Recommended bar diameter for 4140 is 6.5 Inch (165 mm) or less and hollows with wall thickness of 2.75 Inch (70 mm) or less. 4145 Mod steel can be supplied up to 9.5 Inch (241 mm) diameter solid bars in quenched and tempered condition.

1.3 These materials to this specification do not meet the requirements of NACE MR0175/ISO 15156 for hydrogen sulfide service.

1.4 For welding applications, 4145 Mod shall not be used.

1.5 4142 is acceptable for parts that do not require welding.

### 1. Scope:

1.1. This specification is for AISI 4140 / 4145 Mod bars and tubes furnished in pre-heat treated condition, normalized-quench and tempered or quench and tempered to 125 ksi (862 MPa) minimum yield strength.

1.2 Recommended bar diameter for 4140 is 6.0 Inch (152 mm) or less and hollows with wall thickness of 2.5 Inch (63.5) or less. 4145 Mod steel can be supplied up to 8.0 Inch (203 mm) diameter solid bars in quenched and tempered condition.

1.3. These materials to this specification do not meet the requirements of NACE MR0175/ISO 15156 for hydrogen sulfide service.

1.4. Welding of 4145 Mod shall not be allowed, except in specific processes, such as it is allowed when welding a buffer layer on the base metal 4145 steel prior to the hardfacing process.

3.3.1. Bars of 4145 Mod over 8.0 Inch (203 mm) OD must be trepanned prior to heat treatment.

3.3.2. For bars that will trepanned after heat treatment, if mechanical properties meet at the ID location of the component to be made, then re-heat treatment of the trepanned bar is not necessary.

3.3.3. Forging and heavy wall stock under following conditions must be rough machined before heat treatment (Before austenitizing and quenching).

3.3.3.1. Solid bar diameter greater than 6.0 Inch (152 mm) or wall thickness greater than 2.5 Inch (63.5 mm) for 4140 and

3.3.3.2. Solid bar diameter greater than 8.0 Inch (203 mm) or wall thickness greater than 2.5 Inch (63.5 mm) for 4145 Mod.

3.3.4. The quench media shall be 1) Oil, 2) Polymer equivalent cooling rate to oil or 3) Interrupted water quench, water spray or other water equivalent quench practices.

3.3.5. The tempering temperature shall be at the discretion of heat treater to achieve the specification requirements.

**Title:** Seals, FFKM Chemraz, 90 Durometer, Greene Tweed, 510, Unified Specification

## 1. Scope:

1.1. This unified specification is for the production and procurement of compound 510, 90 durometer, FFKM, Chemraz o-rings, v-rings, t-seals or other seal applications manufactured by Greene Tweed. The specification may not be appropriate for other products manufactured using compound 510. It is not to be used for any compound other than 510 or any manufacturer other than Greene Tweed. This specification will replace all previous specifications for Chemraz 510.

1.2. Non-material related requirements such as packaging, labeling, or reporting requirements may be altered by documents attached to the part or purchase order and will take priority over the minimum requirements herein without creating a non-conformance. Site specific or product line specific documents attached to the purchase order or part will likewise take precedence over this specification.

## 2. Requirements:

### 2.1. Material:

All 510 seals shall be molded from compounded stock. The compound is a special perfluoroelastomer compound designated 510 by Greene Tweed. Seals shall be based on a perfluoroelastomer, suitably cured to produce seals meeting the physical and mechanical properties of the required specification. The perfluoroelastomer shall be classified FFKM by ASTM D1418.

### 2.2. Approved Manufacturer and Compound:

Greene Tweed
Kulpsville, Pennsylvania
Compound: 510, 90 durometer Chemraz FFKM

### 2.3. Manufacture:

Seals shall be molded from compounded stock unless specifically approved by Schlumberger engineering. Machining or grinding is not permitted. Extrusion is not permitted except for preforming or unless specifically approved by engineering. Press curing and post curing is required. It is anticipated that these seals will be molded in Pennsylvania.

### 2.4. RoHS and WEEE:

Material shall not contain any element in reportable limits in accordance with the regulations of RoHS and WEEE. The certification should contain a notation that the part complies with these standards.

Note: WEEE is applicable only for Electrical and Electronic parts.

### 2.5. Testing:

2.5.1. Random samples of finished seals or raw material taken according to a sample plan shall conform to the specification requirements when tested according to ASTM D-1414 or to the applicable procedure in so far as practical. Testing for tensile strength and tensile stress is not required on seals which are too small to permit assembly on rollers and are, after cutting, too short to permit testing as a single strand. Eliminating testing for tensile strength does not eliminate testing for elongation; elongation tests can be made by stretching a ring over a mandrel of a size which will stretch the ring sufficiently to produce the required elongation when figured on the I.D. of the ring.

2.6.1. Seals shall be manufactured to ISO3601-1 Class B dimensions and Class B tolerances unless otherwise specified on the appropriate drawing, specification or part description. T-Seal dimensions and tolerances shall be manufactured to the appropriate Greene Tweed catalog or specification.

2.6.2. As received, seals shall be uniform in quality and free of burrs, slivers, nicks, foreign material or other defects considered to be detrimental to the intended use of the product.

### 2.7. Responsibility for Inspection:

The seal supplier shall be responsible for the required dimensional inspections, visual inspections and physical or mechanical property tests. Schlumberger reserves the right to sample and require the supplier to furnish samples as necessary to ensure that the seals conform to the requirements of this specification or other specifications and to evaluate their utility and performance to assure the product is fit for purpose. All visual inspections at the supplier and Schlumberger shall be in accordance with CNMS-6.

**Title:** O-ring, Viton, 95 Durometer, Parco, 9021-95, Unified specification

## 1. Scope:

This unified specification is for the production and procurement of compound 9021-95, 95 durometer, FKM, Viton o-rings manufactured by Parco. The specification may not be appropriate for other products manufactured using compound 9021-95. It is not to be used for any compound other than 9021-95 or any manufacturer other than Parco.

Non-material related requirements such as packaging, labeling, or reporting requirements may be altered by other documents attached to the purchase order and will take priority over those requirements herein without creating a non-conformance.

## 2. Requirements:

### 2.1. Material:
All 9021-95 o-rings shall be molded from compounded stock. The compound is a special fluoroelastomer compound designated 9021-95 by Parco. Parco 9021-95 o-rings shall be based on a fluorocarbon elastomer, suitably cured to produce o-rings rings meeting the physical and mechanical properties of the required specification. The fluorocarbon elastomer shall be classified FKM by ASTM D1418.

### 2.2. Approved Manufacturer and Compound:
Parco
Ontario, California
Compound: 9021-95, 95 Durometer Viton FKM

### 2.3. RoHS & WEEE:
Material shall not contain any element in reportable limits in accordance with the regulations of RoHS or WEEE. The certification should contain a notation that the part complies with these standards

### 2.4. Manufacture:
All o-rings shall be molded from compounded stock. Machining or grinding is not permitted. Extrusion is not permitted except for performing or unless specifically approved by engineering. Press curing and post curing is required.

### 2.5. Testing:
Random samples of finished rings or raw material taken according to a sample plan shall conform to the specification requirements when tested according to ASTM D-1414 or to the applicable procedure in so far as practical. Testing for tensile strength and tensile stress is not required on rings which are too small to permit assembly on rollers and are, after cutting, too short to permit testing as a single strand. Eliminating testing for tensile strength does not eliminate testing for elongation; elongation tests can be made by stretching a ring over a mandrel of a size which will stretch the ring sufficiently to produce the required elongation when figured on the I.D. of the ring.

#### 2.5.1 Physical and mechanical properties for 9021-95 shall conform to these values:

| Property                                         | Requirement | ASTM Spec      |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ----------- | -------------- |
| Tensile Strength, psi minimum                    | 1500        | D-412          |
| Elongation % minimum                             | 85          | D-412          |
| Hardness, Durometer A                            | 95 +/- 5    | D-2240         |
| Compression Set 70 hours at 400°F (204°C), % max | 25          | D-395          |
| Specific Gravity                                 | 1.82-1.88   | D-297 or D-792 |

# Radiographic Examination for Small Diameter Solid Bar Material 0.500 in and under

# 6.0 Personnel

6.1 Personnel performing examination of this procedure shall be qualified and certified NDE Level I, Level II, or Level III in accordance with American Society for Nondestructive Testing SNT-TC-1A.

6.2 Only Level II or Level III personnel shall be allowed to interpret test results.

# 7.0 Surface Preparation

Material surfaces shall satisfy the requirements of the applicable materials specification or referencing Code Section. Additional conditioning if necessary, by any suitable process to such a degree that the resulting radiographic image due to any surface irregularities cannot mask or be confused with the image of any discontinuity.

# 8.0 Backscatter Radiation Check

8.1 A lead shield with minimum dimensions of 1/2-in height and 1/16-in thickness shall be attached to the back of each film holder during each exposure to determine if backscatter radiation is exposing the film.

8.2 Excessive Backscatter is indicated when a light image of the shield shows on the radiograph. A dark image of the shield on a lighter background is not cause for rejection.

# 9.0 System of Identification

All films shall be clearly identified by numbers, letters and/or markers so that the part and the discontinuities in it can be quickly and accurately located. The radiograph shall be traceable to the contract, component and etc. As a minimum each film shall show:

- Job Number
- PART I.D. Number
- Film View Number
- Manufacturer’s I.D. Symbol or Name
- Date
- Name of RT Vendor
- Location Numbers

# 10.0 Monitoring Density Limitations of Radiographs

Either a densitometer or step wedge comparison film shall be used for judging film density. The densitometer/step wedge comparison film shall be calibrated in accordance with the latest edition of the RT Vendor’s quality control policy.

# 11.0 Equipment and Materials

11.1 Radiation Device shall be Iridium-192 radiation source used for radiography of materials tested to this procedure.

11.2 Film shall be Fuji 29 of a size to accommodate the material being examined.

# 4. Requirements

# 4.1 Melt Practice Requirements

The material shall be melted by one of the following sequence of processes either method 1 or method 2.

1. Method 1:
1. Step 1 - Vacuum induction melting (VIM).
2. Step 2 - Vacuum arc remelting (VAR).
3. Optional Step 3 - VAR.
2. Method 2:
1. Step 1: Basic Electric Furnace (EF).
2. Step 2: Either argon oxygen decarburization (AOD) or vacuum oxygen decarburization (VOD).
3. Step 3: Vacuum arc remelting (VAR).
4. Step 4: Additional VAR.

# 4.2 Forging and Hot Working Requirements

The minimum total hot work reduction ratio shall be 4.0:1.

# 4.3 Chemical Composition Requirements

1. The chemical composition for this alloy shall conform to the weight percent requirements specified in Table 1.
2. The chemical composition shall be tested on a remelting ingot basis per ASTM E354, ASTM E1019, ASTM E1473, and ASTM E2465 or a nationally or internationally recognized industry standard.
3. When material is qualified by the use of check (product) analysis performed on either the qualification test coupon (QTC) or a non-critical area of the production material, the analysis shall conform to the check (product) analysis variation specified in ASTM B880.

### 4.4 Heat Treatment Requirements

#### 4.4.1 Heat Treating Equipment Qualification and Calibration

1. The practice for qualification of heat-treating equipment shall be per the API 6A annex for qualification of heat-treating equipment, AMS 2750, or another internationally recognized standard

2. Furnace instrumentation shall be calibrated at least every 3 months with acceptable grace period as defined in AMS 2750 or other internationally recognized standard.

3. Furnaces shall be surveyed no less than once a year. When a furnace is moved, repaired or rebuilt refer to API 6A for survey requirements.

#### 4.4.2 Temperature Monitoring

1. The material temperature shall be measured by use of either a contact surface thermocouple or a heat sink as described in API 6A. The hold time shall not commence

1. The material manufacturer or material supplier shall maintain copies of the heat treating charts showing the material temperature as measured by the contact surface thermocouple or heat sink for 5 years minimum following the date of heat treatment.
2. The loading of the furnace shall allow all material to receive uniform heating and cooling over its entire surface.

# 4.4.3 Solution Annealing and Age Hardening

The production material and QTC(s) shall be solution annealed and age hardened in accordance with following procedure.

Heat treatment shall be performed only by producing mill. Local heat treatment shall be allowed only with written authorization by Schlumberger and following a written procedure.

# 4.4.3.1 Solution Annealing

Solution anneal at temperature 1870⁰F to 1925⁰F (1021⁰C to 1052⁰C), for one (1) hour minimum to two and half (2 ½) hours maximum. Cool in air, inert gas, water, polymer, or oil to ambient temperature.

Note: Air cooling or inert gas cooling of section thickness greater than 3 in. (76 mm) shall only be upon agreement between purchaser, manufacturer and end user.

# 4.4.3.2 Age Hardening

Age harden at temperature 1425⁰F to 1475⁰F (774⁰C to 802⁰C) for six to eight (6 to 8) hours. Cool in air, inert gas, water, polymer or oil to ambient temperature.

# 4.4.4 Re-heat Treatment

1. Complete re-heat treatment is permitted. Alternatively, re-aging within the parameters of section 4.4.3.2 is permitted, provided the cumulative aging time does not exceed the maximum allowable aging time.
2. If the material is re-aged without re-solution annealing, the testing required by 4.5.1, 4.5.2, 4.5.3, 4.5.5 may be performed on remnants of the original QTC, provided the remnants are re-aged with the production material they represent.
3. All other requirements required by 4.5.1, 4.5.2, 4.5.3, 4.5.5 shall be met by material that has been subjected to either of above re-heat treatment steps.

# 4.5 Testing Requirements

# 4.5.1 Tensile Testing Requirements

# 4.5.1.1 Test Location and Frequency

One tensile test shall be performed for each tested QTC. The test frequency shall be one test per remelt ingot per heat treatment lot.

The QT C shall be either a prolongation (full cross-section on thickest end) or sacrificial production part. The microstructural analysis shall be performed on material in the final heat treatment condition. Refer Attachment A-1 for sample locations.

The microstructural samples shall be etched using one of the approved etchants as shown in Attachment B.

# 4.5.5.2 Grain Size Evaluation

1. The average grain size shall be determined in accordance with ASTM E112. The ASTM average grain size shall be No. 2 or finer.
2. No topological duplex grain size, as defined and measured per ASTM E1181, is allowed.

# 4.5.5.3 Deleterious Phases Examination

The microstructural samples shall be examined for deleterious phases at 100X and 500X using light microscopy. The acceptance criteria are as follows:

1. The microstructure shall be free from acicular phases except in individual, isolated grains that are not representative of the bulk microstructure. In no case shall any individual grain be surrounded with acicular phases.
2. The microstructures shall be free from continuous networks of secondary phases along grain boundaries, except for individual, isolated grains or isolated fields of view that are not representative of the bulk microstructure. The presence of discrete, isolated particles of secondary phases or carbides is acceptable.
3. There shall be no Laves phase.

Examples of acceptable and unacceptable microstructures are provided in Attachment C-1 through C-5. These examples are intended to portray the representative microstructure and not worst-case fields, and they do not represent all of the possible precipitation patterns in Alloy 718. Therefore, these examples are not intended to be quantitative standards of cleanliness. C-1 and C-2 are examples of acceptable microstructures. C-3, C-4, and C-5 are examples of unacceptable microstructures.

# 4.5.6 Nondestructive Examination

The material shall be 100% ultrasonically examined and accepted per API 6A PSL Level 4, NDE-31 or equivalent recognized industry standard.

**Title:** O-Ring, FKM 929A, 95A Durometer, Unified Specification

## 1. Scope:

1.1 This specification is for the production and procurement of 95A Durometer O-rings of FKM fluorocarbon rubber. The specification may not be appropriate for other products manufactured using compound 929A. It is not to be used for any compound other than 929A or any manufacturer other than Greene Tweed.

1.2 Non-material related requirements such as packaging, labeling, or reporting requirements may be altered by other documents attached to the purchase order and will take priority over those requirements herein without creating a non-conformance.

## 2. Requirements:

2.1. **Material:** Shall be an elastomer compound, based on a fluorocarbon polymer, suitably cured to produce O-rings meeting the physical and mechanical properties of this specification

2.2. **Approved Manufacturer and Compound:**
   - Manufacturer: Greene Tweed
   - Compound: 929A

2.3. **Manufacture:** All O-rings shall be molded from compounded stock.

2.4. **RoHS and WEEE:** Material shall not contain any element in reportable limits in accordance with the regulations of RoHS and WEEE. The certification should contain a notation that the part complies with these standards.

2.5. **Testing:**

   2.5.1 Random samples of finished rings or raw material taken according to a sample plan shall be checked against specification requirements when tested according to ASTM D-1414 or to the applicable procedure in so far as practical.

   2.5.2 Testing for tensile strength and tensile stress is not required on rings which are too small to permit assembly on rollers and are, after cutting, too short to permit testing as a single strand.

   2.5.3 Eliminating testing for tensile strength does not eliminate testing for elongation; elongation tests can be made by stretching a ring over a mandrel of a size which will stretch the ring sufficiently to produce the required elongation when figured on the I.D. of the ring.

   2.5.4 Physical and mechanical properties for 929A shall conform to below requirements:

| Property                                                  | Requirement | ASTM Spec      |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | -------------- |
| Tensile Strength, psi min.                                | 2300        | D-412          |
| %Elongation, min.                                         | 15          | D-412          |
| Hardness, Durometer A                                     | 95 ± 5      | D-2240         |
| Compression Set 22 hours at 300°F (149°C), In Air, % max. | 35          | D-395 Method B |
| Specific gravity                                          | 1.81 ± 0.03 | D-297 or D-792 |

SUBJECT: Procedure for bonded seal elastomer tear off test

## 1.0 Scope

The specification covers preparation steps, test fixture, test procedure, and acceptance criteria for the bonded seals tear off test. The test objective is evaluation of rubber bonding quality in the completed product.

## 2.0 Witness samples quantity

### 2.1

Witness samples is the quantity of bonded seals that must be additionally manufactured for each of bonded seals manufacturing batch and during the same batch manufacturing process timeline.

### 2.2

All witness samples must be exposed to elastomer tear off test. The quantity of witness samples is determined based on manufacturing batch size and is stated in Table 1. In general, for each batch of fifty (50) seals or less two (2) witness seals have to be additionally built to be used for tear off test. Witness samples to be selected at random from manufacturing batch.

### Table 1. Witness samples quantity (reference is ISO 2859-1)

| Manufacturing batch size | Quantity of witness samples (bonded seals) |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
| up to 50                 | 2                                          |
| from 51 to 90            | 3                                          |
| from 91 to 150           | 4                                          |
| from 151 to 280          | 6                                          |
| from 281 to 500          | 10                                         |
| from 501 to 1200         | 16                                         |


### 2.3

All witness samples being tested per the PO must be shipped to Schlumberger with the complete order or Pictures of the witness samples should be included in the CoC and physical parts should be kept by manufacturer for at least 3 years.

## 1.0 Purpose:
This specification provides the standard methods for Rockwell hardness and Rockwell Superficial Hardness of metallic materials as performed by Schlumberger [SLB]. Original mills and suppliers will use their in-house procedure, which complies with ASTM E18.

N/A

N/A

### 5.1 Qualification Requirements:
N/A

Hardness inspection is performed when required by inspection procedures, engineering drawings, shop routings, heat treatment and material specifications, and customer quality plan.

Standardized test blocks used to check the accuracy of the machine must be within 15 Rockwell points of the hardness that the testing machine is expected to measure.

##### 5.4.2.3
Standardized test blocks shall not be ground or resurfaced at any time.

# 5.4.2 Indentations

5.4.2.4 Indentations must be spaced greater than 2-1/2 diameters from its center to the edge of the specimen or 3 diameters from another indentation measured center to center.

5.4.2.5 Hardness readings may only be taken on the one side that is marked by the manufacturer of the standardized test block.

# 5.4.3 Accuracy Check

The accuracy of the Rockwell testing machine shall be checked upon first use by the operator when used, unless previously checked on the same calendar date. This check must be documented in the hardness log. A printable documentation record form is included on the last page of this procedure. The log can be either a hard copy or an electronic spreadsheet stored in a shared file as long as its revision controlled.

# 5.4.3.1 Preliminary Indentations

Before making the check, make at least two preliminary indentations to ensure that the hardness testing machine is working freely and that the test block and indenter, and anvil are seated correctly. The results of these preliminary indentations will not be used to obtain the averaged reading.

# 5.4.3.2 Hardness Readings

Next make at least three hardness readings on a standardized hardness test block on the scale and at the hardness level at which the machine is being used. If two indentations are closer than three diameters to one another, the punch is void. This does not void the test block. Continue using the same test block to verify the accuracy. If the mean (average) of these values falls within the tolerances marked on the standardized hardness test block, the machine may be regarded as satisfactory.

# 5.4.3.3 Indenter Storage

After the indenter has been removed from the hardness testing machine, it will need to be stored back to its proper storage case.

# 5.4.3.4 Indenter Installation

Any time the indenter installs into the hardness testing machine, it will require a minimum two preliminary indentations to ensure that the hardness testing machine is working freely and that the test block, indenter and anvil are seated correctly. The results of these preliminary indentations will not be used to obtain the averaged reading.

# 5.4.3.5 Indenter Change

When removing an HRc indenter and inserting another HRc indenter to the hardness testing machine, it will require a restart of the hardness readings. A minimum two preliminary indentations to ensure that the hardness testing machine is working freely and that the test block, indenter and anvil are seated correctly.

5.4.4 Procedure for Rockwell Hardness Testing:

5.4.4.1 The surface of the material being tested must be clean, dry and free from scale, pits, and foreign material that might crush or flow under test pressure and adversely affect the hardness reading. All de-carb should be removed from the test surface.

5.4.4.2 The hardness test operator must choose the proper Rockwell scale for testing the product. The following general rules apply in choosing the proper scale.

- Rockwell C scale is the preferred scale for all materials that have over a .125" wall or through thickness. Rockwell C scale cannot be used on materials with less than a 20 Rockwell C hardness value.

- Rockwell B scale is used on all materials with a Rockwell B hardness value of 100 or less (Rockwell C less than 20). Rockwell B scale must be used for brass.

- Rockwell A scale is used when the material is under .125" wall or for any other reason Rockwell B or C scale cannot be used. Note it is not advisable to test cylindrical parts with .125" or less wall thickness as they can deflect or be deformed if this test is performed.

5.4.4.3 Take three hardness readings on the part being tested using the hardness template as shown in Appendix A. If the mean (average) of these values are within the tolerances of the specification after using the appropriate conversion chart the part is regarded as satisfactory. Refer to Appendix B on how to use the Hardness Template.

In bringing the penetrator and the test specimen into contact, avoid all sudden impact. The last movement of the elevating or lowering screw shall always be in a direction that will bring penetrator and test specimen together. Apply the major load by tripping the operating lever without shock. Remove the major load by bringing the operating lever back to its latched position within 2 to 3 seconds after its motion has stopped.

# 5.4.4.7

Take the Rockwell hardness as the reading of the pointer on the dial after the major load has been removed and while the minor load is still applied. These readings are sometimes estimated to one half of a division or to one tenth of a division, depending on the material being tested. Repeat two more times for a total of three readings. The average of the three shall be recorded as the hardness reading.

# 5.4.4.8

The operator will document the results of the hardness test using the following guidelines:

- (hardness reading) followed by HRc for C scale
- (hardness reading) followed by HRb for B scale
- (hardness reading) followed by HRa for A scale

When using a carbide ball for HRB, the inspector should place a W after the hardness reading. When using a steel ball, the inspector should place a “ after the hardness reading. Per ASTM E18-20, a tungsten carbide ball is considered the standard type of Rockwell Indenter ball. Steel ball indenters may be used only for testing thin sheet tin mill products using the HR15T and HR30T scales with a diamond spot anvil.

# 5.4.4.9

Hardness measurements exceeding the acceptance criteria are acceptable if the average of three readings taken within close proximity do not exceed the maximum limit and no individual reading is greater than 2 HRc (or equivalent) points above the acceptance criteria.

## Title: Glass Filled PEEK, Polyetheretherketone Polymer

2.3.1 Parts for all applications shall be direct injection molded or machined from injection-molded stock or stock made by the Dynamic Cast Molding System.

2.3.2 Extrusion is an acceptable process for large OD blank material, which will eventually be machined where injection molding is not applicable.

### 2.4 RoHS and WEEE:

Material shall not contain any element in reportable limits in accordance with the regulations of RoHS and WEEE. The certification should contain a notation that the part complies with these standards.

Note: WEEE is applicable only for Electrical and Electronic parts.

### 2.5 Testing:

2.5.1 Physical and Mechanical Properties shall conform to:

| Property                                | Requirement | Standard   |
| --------------------------------------- | ----------- | ---------- |
| Tensile Strength at break, psi, Min     | 14,000      | ASTM D-638 |
| Elongation at break, %, Min             | 2.0         | ASTM D-638 |
| Flexural Modulus @73°F (23°C), psi, Min | 600,000     | ASTM D-790 |
| Specific Gravity, Min                   | 1.40        | ASTM D-792 |


### 2.6 Inspection Acceptability Parameters:

2.6.1 All machined surfaces shall meet the requirements of the engineering drawing.

2.6.2 As received, products shall be free of burrs, slivers, nicks, foreign material, inclusions, separations and other defects considered to be detrimental to the intended use of the product.

### 2.7 Responsibility for Inspection:

The supplier shall be responsible for the required dimensional inspections, visual inspections and physical or mechanical property tests. Schlumberger reserves the right to sample and require the supplier to furnish samples as necessary to ensure that the material conforms to the requirements of this specification or other specifications and to evaluate their utility and performance to assure the product is fit for purpose. All visual inspections at the supplier or at Schlumberger shall be in accordance with 101344397, Visual Inspection of Plastic Seal Components.

### 2.8 Classification of Tests:

2.8.1 Acceptance tests are to be performed by the supplier on each batch to determine conformance to paragraph 2.5.

2.8.1.1 Specific Gravity
2.8.1.2 Tensile Strength
2.8.1.3 Elongation
2.8.1.4 Flexural Modulus

2.8.2 Pre-production tests are to be conducted by the supplier to determine conformance to all technical requirements of this specification and shall be performed on first article materials only.

# 2.9 Qualification:

2.9.1 The vendor shall establish, for each part number supplied, parameters for the process control factors that will produce components meeting the technical requirements of this specification. These shall constitute the qualified procedure and shall be used for manufacturing production parts. If changes become necessary, the vendor shall submit for re-qualification a statement of the proposed changes in material or processing. Production parts incorporating the revised procedures shall not be shipped prior to the receipt of re-qualification.

2.9.2 Process control factors include, but are not limited to:

- 2.9.2.1 Μolding Ρrocedures
- 2.9.2.2 Μachining Ρrocedures
- 2.9.2.3 Ιnspection Μethods

2.9.3 Variations of ±10% are allowed in time, temperature and pressure controls.

2.9.4 Ρroprietary control factors may be assigned a code designation. Variations shall be assigned a modified code.

# 2.10 Μarking and Packing:

2.10.1 Ρackaging: Parts made from this material shall be packaged in standard commercial containers so constructed as to ensure acceptance by common or other carriers for safe transportation at the lowest rate to the point of delivery, unless otherwise specified.

2.10.2 Components shall be packaged in such a manner that they are adequately protected against mechanical damage due to handling and shipping. Each package shall bear the trade name or material, manufacturer's name, lot or batch number, purchase order number, part number and quantity.

2.10.3 Components of different part numbers, sizes, lots or batches shall not be packaged together. No package shall contain in excess of 100 parts.

2.10.4 Μanufacturer's identification markings on any component shall not be permitted without the written consent of the materials engineering department.

2.10.5 Εach shipping container shall be marked in accordance with the current D.O.Τ. regulations outlined in 49 CFR 172.300, as well as current OSHΑ regulations outlined in 29CFR 1910.1200.

2.10.6 Ιdentification: Packages or labels shall have the following information:

- 2.10.6.1 Schlumberger

- 2.10.6.3 Schlumberger Ρurchase Order number and line-item number
- 2.10.6.4 Μanufacturer

## 4. Documentation and Retention:

The following documentation is required to be supplied with each delivery. All required information can be supplied on one certificate or separate certificates at the supplier's discretion. This is considered the minimum requirement, but other documents attached to the part record or purchase order may take priority over these requirements.

4.1 Quality requirements as stipulated on the purchase order and in accordance with site specific quality requirements attached to the purchase order.

4.2 A statement of compliance with RoHS and WEEE.

4.3 A certified test report showing actual data received in the performance of test stipulated in this specification.

4.4 All certifications, test reports and product identification must include the information referenced in the supplier requirements documents that are part of the purchase order

4.5 Noncompliance with any part of the requirements of the specifications, determined by review of the submitted certification and documentation or inspection, will be considered cause for rejection of the entire order. The vendor or supplier is responsible for the supply or retention of all documentation required by the procurement documentation with each delivery.
